candidates.statement: This guidance also specifies the technical requirements and the process of transmission of Safety and Acknowledgement Messages through the B2B g ateway and describes the obligations that stakeholders must adhere to in this process to en sure successful electronic communication. The Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) process is based on the electronic exchange of a Safety Message
candidates.context: • ISO/HL7 27953 - 2:2011 - Health informatics — Individual case safety reports (ICSRs) in pharmacovigilance — Part 2: Human pharmaceutical reporting requirements for ICSR Swissmedic finished the changeover of the reporting process for ICSRs from E2B(R2) to E2B(R3) on the B2B gateway by 30 June 2026 . The transition included the recommendations and procedures of the European Medicines Agency regarding data elements and message specifications (see 11.2 Relevant documents) . Differences in the requirements between the EMA and Swissmedic will be addressed in c hapter 5 of this document. MU101_20_832_MB - Merkblatt | 2.0 | 01.08.2026 5 /21 between a Sender and a Receiver. candidates.statement: To be valid for reporting to Swissmedic , an ICSR must fulfil four minimum reporting criteria: an identifiable reporter, an identifiable patient, a reaction and a suspected medicinal product.
candidates.context: MU101_20_832_MB - Merkblatt | 2.0 | 01.08.2026 8 /21 This note for guidance does not apply to SUSARs of investigational medicinal products (IMPs) or SUSARs/other reportable reactions of AxMPs that do not meet the criteria specified above. Patient identifiers according to EMA: With regard to patients , a t least one patient identifier is required to indicate that a patient exists. This is met through the completion of at least one of the following data elements ICH E2B (R3) D.1, D.1.1.1, D.1.1.2, D.1.1.3, D.1.1.4, D.2.1, D.2.2A, D.2.2.1a, D.2.3 or D.5. At least one of these patient identifier data elements should be different from “UNK”, “ASKU” or “NASK” , since these nullflavors in any of the patient identifier data elements do not indicate that a patient exists. Similarly, use of a text string ‘UNK’ in the patient initials do not indicate the existence of a patient.

For ICSRs arising from literature, the adequate/correct reference must be placed in the section C.4.r./C.4.r.1 (literature reference). For all submitted literature articles, the literature reference (data element C.4.r.1) must be formatted exclusively using the Vancouver citation style. This requirement applies without exception and must be adhered to across all submissions, regardless of source type (journal article, book, conference proceeding or electronic publication). The article itself should be attac hed as a document to the ICSR (see chapter 5.3).

The maximum total size of an ICSR is currently 20 MB. For attachments, a maximum size of 15 MB applies. This adjustment aligns with the regulatory requirements of the EMA and must be taken into account in both the technical and procedural implementation by pharmaceutical companies.

candidates.statement: 5.5 Important n otes MAHs are advised to reduce the number of follow - ups to a minimum; only new and medical ly relevant information such as outcome, alternative medical conditions, other suspect drugs, results of performed investigations or any other data with an impact on causality should trigger follow - up information. Ideally , an initial case should be followed by one follow - up when the case is closed.

In this case no Acknowledgement Message will be returned. Senders of ICSRs should monitor for the absence of a receipt of acknowledgment . In this case contact
candidates.context: If , during the process of parsing the ICSR , the Swissmedic drug safety system can detect a valid sender identifier, an Acknowledgement Message will be created and sent to the sender, listing the detected error. The Transmission Acknowledgement Code reported in the data element ICH E2B(R3) ACK.A.4 will be ‘AR’ , i.e. no data extracted. If the process of parsing the ICSR is successful and the Swissmedic drug safety system cannot detect a valid receiver identifier, an Acknowledgement Message will be created and sent to the sender, listing the detected error. The Transmission Acknowledgement Code reported in the data element ICH E2B(R3) ACK.A.4 will be ‘AR’ , i.e. no data extracted.

candidates.statement: 8.2.2 Security a spects To facilitate the secure transmission of safety and acknowledgement messages over the Internet, each party must purchase, install and operate applications that allow for the successful transmission and receipt of encrypted and digitally signed safety and acknowledgement messages via the Swissmedic g ateway.
candidates.context: MU101_20_832_MB - Merkblatt | 2.0 | 01.08.2026 19 /21 The applications chosen by each party must provide the essential functionality and interoperability as outlined in chapter 6.

Encrypting and digitally signing safety and acknowledgement messages by using certificates provides the parties with assurance about each transaction.
